﴿God originates creation, then repeats it, then to Him you will be returned﴾. ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will be dismayed﴾.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: they will be made joyful, and from this it is said: every hibrah is followed by an 'ibrah. Al-'Ajjaj said:

"So praise be to God, who gave the hibr
to the allies of truth; indeed the ally is grateful."

That is, joy. Some of them said: the hibrah in the language is every good blessing. Al-tahbir is beautification, and from it the ink is called hibr, because the pages are beautified with it. Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, from Hamid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Yunus, from Rawh, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, regarding ﴿in a meadow, they will be delighted﴾, that he said: "Listening (to music) in Paradise."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Abdullah ibn Shanbah, from Umayr ibn Mirdas, from Salamah ibn Shabib, from Abd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I heard al-Awza'i say regarding ﴿in a meadow, they will be delighted﴾: "Listening." And he said: when listening begins, no tree in Paradise remains except that it rustles. And from him, from Salamah ibn Shabib, from Dawud ibn al-Jarrah al-Asqalani, who said: I heard al-Awza'i say: "None of those whom God created has a more beautiful voice than Israfil. When he begins listening, he cuts off the prayers and glorification of the people of the seven heavens."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dinawari informed us, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Majah al-Qazwini, from al-Hasan ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn 'Arad al-Shaybani, who both said: al-Qasim ibn Mutayyab al-'Ijli informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Paradise has one hundred degrees; between each two degrees is what is between the heaven and the earth. Al-Firdaws is the highest of them in elevation and the middle of them in place, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth, and above it the Throne will be placed on the Day of Resurrection." (Musnad Ahmad: 5/321; Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/82.)

A man stood up to him and said: "O Messenger of God, I am a man to whom voice is beloved; is there a beautiful voice in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, by the One in whose hand is my soul. God, glory be to Him, will reveal to a tree in Paradise: 'Make my servants who occupied themselves with my worship and remembrance hear (the sound), away from the strumming of lutes and the flutes.' Then it will raise a voice that the creatures have never heard the like of, of glorifying and sanctifying the Lord."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Harun, from Muhammad ibn Harun al-'Attar, from Hazim ibn Yahya al-Halawani, from al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik, from Masruh al-Harrani, from Sulayman ibn 'Ata', from Salamah ibn Abdullah al-Juhani, from his paternal uncle, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to admonish the people, and he mentioned Paradise and what is in it of spouses and blessings. At the back of the people was a Bedouin, who knelt on his knees and said: "O Messenger of God, is there any listening in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, O Bedouin. In Paradise there is a river whose banks are virgins of every fair-skinned, slender-waisted kind, who sing with voices the creatures have never heard the like of. That is the best bliss of the people of Paradise." (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 14/13.)

He said: I asked Abu al-Darda': "With what will they sing?" He said: "With glorification, God willing." He said: al-Khawsaniyyah is the one whose upper part is slender and whose lower part is full.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadhani, from Ali ibn Sa'id al-'Askari, who said: Abu Badr 'Abbad ibn al-Walid al-Ghubari informed me, from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khurasani, from Abdullah ibn 'Arada al-Shaybani, from al-Qasim ibn Mutayyab, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: "In Paradise there are trees upon which are bells of silver. When the people of Paradise wish to listen, God, Mighty and Majestic, sends a wind from beneath the Throne, which falls upon those trees, and it moves those bells with sounds that, if the people of the earth heard them, would die of delight." (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 14/13.)

Al-Husayn informed me, from Abu Shanbah and Abdullah ibn Yusuf, who both said: Muhammad ibn 'Imran said, from Muhammad ibn Mansur, who said: Yahya ibn Abi al-Hajjaj informed me, from Abdullah ibn Muslim, from a client of the Banu Umayyah called Sulayman, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah being asked: "Is there any listening for the people of Paradise?"

He said: "Yes. There is a tree whose root is of gold, whose branches are of silver, and whose fruit is pearls, chrysolite and rubies. God, glory be to Him and exalted, sends a wind that makes its parts strike one another, and no one has ever heard anything more beautiful than it."

His saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought to punishment﴾. ﴿So exalted is God﴾, pray to God ﴿when you enter the evening﴾, which is the prayer of 'Asr and Maghrib, ﴿and when you enter the morning﴾, which is the prayer of Fajr. ﴿And to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth﴾, ﴿and in the late afternoon﴾, which is the prayer of 'Isha' al-Akhirah, meaning: glorify Him in the late afternoon, ﴿and when you reach noon﴾, which is the prayer of Zuhr.

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, from [in another copy: from Abu al-Sharqi], from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Hafiz, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, who said: Nafi' ibn al-Azraq said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Do you find the five prayers in the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes: ﴿So exalted is God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ … to His saying: ﴿and when you reach noon﴾."

(Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/493, no. 5076.)

And when he dies, there will be recorded for him, for each good deed, ten good deeds in his grave." (Al-Bihar: 83/18.)

A man stood up to him and said: "O Messenger of God, I am a man to whom voice is beloved; is there a beautiful voice in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, by the One in whose hand is my soul. God, glory be to Him, will reveal to a tree in Paradise: 'Make my servants who occupied themselves with my worship and remembrance hear (the sound), away from the strumming of lutes and the flutes.' Then it will raise a voice that the creatures have never heard the like of, of glorifying and sanctifying the Lord."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Harun, from Muhammad ibn Harun al-'Attar, from Hazim ibn Yahya al-Halawani, from al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik, from Masruh al-Harrani, from Sulayman ibn 'Ata', from Salamah ibn Abdullah al-Juhani, from his paternal uncle, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to admonish the people, and he mentioned Paradise and what is in it of spouses and blessings. At the back of the people was a Bedouin, who knelt on his knees and said: "O Messenger of God, is there any listening in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, O Bedouin. In Paradise there is a river whose banks are virgins of every fair-skinned, slender-waisted kind, who sing with voices the creatures have never heard the like of. That is the best bliss of the people of Paradise." (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 14/13.)

He said: I asked Abu al-Darda': "With what will they sing?" He said: "With glorification, God willing." He said: al-Khawsaniyyah is the one whose upper part is slender and whose lower part is full.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadhani, from Ali ibn Sa'id al-'Askari, who said: Abu Badr 'Abbad ibn al-Walid al-Ghubari informed me, from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khurasani, from Abdullah ibn 'Arada al-Shaybani, from al-Qasim ibn Mutayyab, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: "In Paradise there are trees upon which are bells of silver. When the people of Paradise wish to listen, God, Mighty and Majestic, sends a wind from beneath the Throne, which falls upon those trees, and it moves those bells with sounds that, if the people of the earth heard them, would die of delight." (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 14/13.)

Al-Husayn informed me, from Abu Shanbah and Abdullah ibn Yusuf, who both said: Muhammad ibn 'Imran said, from Muhammad ibn Mansur, who said: Yahya ibn Abi al-Hajjaj informed me, from Abdullah ibn Muslim, from a client of the Banu Umayyah called Sulayman, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah being asked: "Is there any listening for the people of Paradise?"

He said: "Yes. There is a tree whose root is of gold, whose branches are of silver, and whose fruit is pearls, chrysolite and rubies. God, glory be to Him and exalted, sends a wind that makes its parts strike one another, and no one has ever heard anything more beautiful than it."

His saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought to punishment﴾. ﴿So exalted is God﴾, pray to God ﴿when you enter the evening﴾, which is the prayer of 'Asr and Maghrib, ﴿and when you enter the morning﴾, which is the prayer of Fajr. ﴿And to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth﴾, ﴿and in the late afternoon﴾, which is the prayer of 'Isha' al-Akhirah, meaning: glorify Him in the late afternoon, ﴿and when you reach noon﴾, which is the prayer of Zuhr.

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, from [in another copy: from Abu al-Sharqi], from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Hafiz, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, who said: Nafi' ibn al-Azraq said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Do you find the five prayers in the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes: ﴿So exalted is God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ … to His saying: ﴿and when you reach noon﴾."

Abu Bakr ibn 'Abdus narrated to us, who said: Abu Bakr al-Sharqi narrated to me, who said: Abu Hatim al-Razi narrated to me, who said: Abu Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, narrated to me, al-Layth narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Salmani, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever says when he enters the morning, ﴿So exalted is God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ … to His saying: ﴿thus you will be brought out﴾, he will catch up with what he missed in his day, and whoever says it when he enters the evening will catch up with what he missed in his night." (Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/493, no. 5076.)

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Ahmad informed me, saying: Umar ibn Ahmad ibn Uthman al-Baghdadi wrote to me that Zayd ibn Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Qurashi narrated to them, from Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb, from my paternal uncle, from al-Madi ibn Muhammad, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says: 'Glory be to God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning' — these three verses from Surat al-Rum and the end of Surat al-Saffat — after every prayer he prays, there will be recorded for him good deeds equal to the number of the stars of the sky, the drops of rain, the leaves of trees and the grains of earth's dust. And when he dies, there will be recorded for him, for each good deed, ten good deeds in his grave." (Al-Bihar: 83/18.)

(Surat al-Saffat: 180–182; Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/639, with variation.)

﴿God would not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾. ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst﴾, meaning the outcome that will distress them, which is the Fire. It was said that al-Su'a is a name for Jahannam, just as al-Husna is a name for Paradise.

He said: Yes, I recognize it, and it has become dismayed."

Al-Husayn informed me, from Abu Shanbah and Abdullah ibn Yusuf, who both said: Muhammad ibn 'Imran said, from Muhammad ibn Mansur, who said: Yahya ibn Abi al-Hajjaj informed me, from Abdullah ibn Muslim, from a client of the Banu Umayyah called Sulayman, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah being asked: "Is there any listening for the people of Paradise?"

He said: "Yes. There is a tree whose root is of gold, whose branches are of silver, and whose fruit is pearls, chrysolite and rubies. God, glory be to Him and exalted, sends a wind that makes its parts strike one another, and no one has ever heard anything more beautiful than it."

His saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought to punishment﴾. ﴿So exalted is God﴾, pray to God ﴿when you enter the evening﴾, which is the prayer of 'Asr and Maghrib, ﴿and when you enter the morning﴾, which is the prayer of Fajr. ﴿And to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth﴾, ﴿and in the late afternoon﴾, which is the prayer of 'Isha' al-Akhirah, meaning: glorify Him in the late afternoon, ﴿and when you reach noon﴾, which is the prayer of Zuhr.

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, from [in another copy: from Abu al-Sharqi], from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Hafiz, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, who said: Nafi' ibn al-Azraq said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Do you find the five prayers in the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes: ﴿So exalted is God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ … to His saying: ﴿and when you reach noon﴾."

(Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/493, no. 5076.)

And when he dies, there will be recorded for him, for each good deed, ten good deeds in his grave." (Al-Bihar: 83/18.)

(Surat al-Saffat: 180–182; Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/639, with variation.)

﴿and they cultivated it more than these have cultivated it, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they did not believe﴾, so God, Mighty and Majestic, destroyed them.

﴿God would not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾. ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst﴾, meaning the outcome that will distress them, which is the Fire. It was said that al-Su'a is a name for Jahannam, just as al-Husna is a name for Paradise.

It was also said that the explanation of al-Su'a is what follows it, namely His saying ﴿that they denied﴾, meaning: then the end of the evildoers was denial, as those evil deeds led them to deny ﴿the signs of God and to mock them﴾, that is, they mocked them.

He said: Yes, I recognize it, and it has become dismayed."

Abu Bakr ibn 'Abdus narrated to us, who said: Abu Bakr al-Sharqi narrated to me, who said: Abu Hatim al-Razi narrated to me, who said: Abu Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, narrated to me, al-Layth narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Salmani, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever says when he enters the morning, ﴿So exalted is God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ … to His saying: ﴿thus you will be brought out﴾, he will catch up with what he missed in his day, and whoever says it when he enters the evening will catch up with what he missed in his night." (Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/493, no. 5076.)

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Ahmad informed me, saying: Umar ibn Ahmad ibn Uthman al-Baghdadi wrote to me that Zayd ibn Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Qurashi narrated to them, from Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb, from my paternal uncle, from al-Madi ibn Muhammad, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says: 'Glory be to God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning' — these three verses from Surat al-Rum and the end of Surat al-Saffat — after every prayer he prays, there will be recorded for him good deeds equal to the number of the stars of the sky, the drops of rain, the leaves of trees and the grains of earth's dust. And when he dies, there will be recorded for him, for each good deed, ten good deeds in his grave." (Al-Bihar: 83/18.)

Abdullah ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Shanbah, Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan and al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl, who said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Bahram al-Zanjani informed us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf ibn Qutaybah ibn Muslim, from Bishr ibn al-Husayn, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is pleased that he be measured for with the full measure, let him say: 'Glory be to God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning' … to His saying: ﴿thus you will be brought out﴾, ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe﴾ … to His saying: ﴿And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾." (Surat al-Saffat: 180–182; Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/639, with variation.)

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ghaffar, from Habbarah ibn al-Mughallis, from Kathir, from al-Dahhak, who said: Whoever says "Glory be to God when you enter the evening" up to the end of the verse, he will have a reward equal to the freeing of two hundred slaves from the descendants of Isma'il (peace be upon him).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Shanbah [in another copy: from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Mahan, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi], from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tayalisi [in the copy of Isfahan: al-Tanafisi], from Yahya ibn Adam, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd al-'Ammi, from Muhammad ibn Wasi', from Ka'b, who said: "Whoever says when he enters the morning: 'Glory be to God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning,' up to the end of the verse, no good that occurs in his day will escape him, and no evil that occurs in it will reach him. And whoever says it when he enters the evening, no evil that occurs in his night will reach him, and no good that occurs in his night will escape him." [In the copy of Isfahan: "in his day."] (Ibid.) And Ibrahim, the Friend of God (peace be upon him), used to say it six times every day and night.

﴿Have they not reflected within themselves? God did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and for a specified term﴾. He means: until a known time, when they reach it and perish, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Indeed, many of the people are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord﴾. ﴿Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them, who were greater than them in strength, and who stirred up the earth﴾, meaning they plowed it, turned it over for cultivation and construction,

﴿and they cultivated it more than these have cultivated it, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they did not believe﴾, so God, Mighty and Majestic, destroyed them.

﴿God would not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾. ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst﴾, meaning the outcome that will distress them, which is the Fire. It was said that al-Su'a is a name for Jahannam, just as al-Husna is a name for Paradise.

﴿That they denied﴾, meaning "because they denied." It was also said that the explanation of al-Su'a is what follows it, namely His saying ﴿that they denied﴾, meaning: then the end of the evildoers was denial, as those evil deeds led them to deny ﴿the signs of God and to mock them﴾, that is, they mocked them.

﴿God originates creation, then repeats it, then to Him you will be returned﴾. ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will be dismayed﴾.

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid, who said: "yublisu" means "they will be grieved." Abu Yahya narrated from him: "they will be disgraced." Qatadah, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it is with two yas. Ibn Zayd said: the mublis is one upon whom calamity and evil have descended. Al-Farra' said: their speech and arguments will be cut off. Abu 'Ubaydah said: they will regret, and he recited:

"O friend, do you recognize a worn-out traced ruin?
He said: Yes, I recognize it, and it has become dismayed."

(Al-Sihah of al-Jawhari: 3/909.)

Al-Sulami read yubalasu with a fatha on the lam, but the first reading is better. ﴿And they will have no intercessors from their partners﴾, meaning their idols that they worshipped besides God, to intercede for them, ﴿and they will be disbelievers in their partners﴾, denying them and disowning them.

﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, on that Day they will be separated﴾. ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a meadow, a garden, delighted﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: they will be honored. Mujahid and Qatadah said: they will be given blessings. Abu 'Ubaydah said: they will be made joyful, and from this it is said: every hibrah is followed by an 'ibrah. Al-'Ajjaj said:

"So praise be to God, who gave the hibr
to the allies of truth; indeed the ally is grateful."

That is, joy. Some of them said: the hibrah in the language is every good blessing. Al-tahbir is beautification, and from it the ink is called hibr, because the pages are beautified with it. The scholar is called hibr because he is characterized by good character. The poet said: "the scribe of Himyar beautifies it." It was also said: yuhbarun means they are made to enjoy listening.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, from Hamid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Yunus, from Rawh, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, regarding ﴿in a meadow, they will be delighted﴾, that he said: "Listening (to music) in Paradise."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Abdullah ibn Shanbah, from Umayr ibn Mirdas, from Salamah ibn Shabib, from Abd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I heard al-Awza'i say regarding ﴿in a meadow, they will be delighted﴾: "Listening." And he said: when listening begins, no tree in Paradise remains except that it rustles. And from him, from Salamah ibn Shabib, from Dawud ibn al-Jarrah al-Asqalani, who said: I heard al-Awza'i say: "None of those whom God created has a more beautiful voice than Israfil. When he begins listening, he cuts off the prayers and glorification of the people of the seven heavens."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dinawari informed us, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Majah al-Qazwini, from al-Hasan ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn 'Arad al-Shaybani, who both said: al-Qasim ibn Mutayyab al-'Ijli informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Paradise has one hundred degrees; between each two degrees is what is between the heaven and the earth. Al-Firdaws is the highest of them in elevation and the middle of them in place, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth, and above it the Throne will be placed on the Day of Resurrection." (Musnad Ahmad: 5/321; Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/82.)

A man stood up to him and said: "O Messenger of God, I am a man to whom voice is beloved; is there a beautiful voice in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, by the One in whose hand is my soul. God, glory be to Him, will reveal to a tree in Paradise: 'Make my servants who occupied themselves with my worship and remembrance hear (the sound), away from the strumming of lutes and the flutes.' Then it will raise a voice that the creatures have never heard the like of, of glorifying and sanctifying the Lord."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Harun, from Muhammad ibn Harun al-'Attar, from Hazim ibn Yahya al-Halawani, from al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik, from Masruh al-Harrani, from Sulayman ibn 'Ata', from Salamah ibn Abdullah al-Juhani, from his paternal uncle, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to admonish the people, and he mentioned Paradise and what is in it of spouses and blessings. At the back of the people was a Bedouin, who knelt on his knees and said: "O Messenger of God, is there any listening in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, O Bedouin. In Paradise there is a river whose banks are virgins of every fair-skinned, slender-waisted kind, who sing with voices the creatures have never heard the like of. That is the best bliss of the people of Paradise." (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 14/13.)

He said: I asked Abu al-Darda': "With what will they sing?" He said: "With glorification, God willing." He said: al-Khawsaniyyah is the one whose upper part is slender and whose lower part is full.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadhani, from Ali ibn Sa'id al-'Askari, who said: Abu Badr 'Abbad ibn al-Walid al-Ghubari informed me, from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khurasani, from Abdullah ibn 'Arada al-Shaybani, from al-Qasim ibn Mutayyab, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: "In Paradise there are trees upon which are bells of silver. When the people of Paradise wish to listen, God, Mighty and Majestic, sends a wind from beneath the Throne, which falls upon those trees, and it moves those bells with sounds that, if the people of the earth heard them, would die of delight." (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 14/13.)

He said: "Yes. There is a tree whose root is of gold, whose branches are of silver, and whose fruit is pearls, chrysolite and rubies. God, glory be to Him and exalted, sends a wind that makes its parts strike one another, and no one has ever heard anything more beautiful than it."

Abdullah ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Shanbah, Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan and al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl, who said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Bahram al-Zanjani informed us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf ibn Qutaybah ibn Muslim, from Bishr ibn al-Husayn, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is pleased that he be measured for with the full measure, let him say: 'Glory be to God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning' … to His saying: ﴿thus you will be brought out﴾, ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe﴾ … to His saying: ﴿And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾." (Surat al-Saffat: 180–182; Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/639, with variation.)

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ghaffar, from Habbarah ibn al-Mughallis, from Kathir, from al-Dahhak, who said: Whoever says "Glory be to God when you enter the evening" up to the end of the verse, he will have a reward equal to the freeing of two hundred slaves from the descendants of Isma'il (peace be upon him).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Shanbah [in another copy: from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Mahan, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi], from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tayalisi [in the copy of Isfahan: al-Tanafisi], from Yahya ibn Adam, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd al-'Ammi, from Muhammad ibn Wasi', from Ka'b, who said: "Whoever says when he enters the morning: 'Glory be to God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning,' up to the end of the verse, no good that occurs in his day will escape him, and no evil that occurs in it will reach him. And whoever says it when he enters the evening, no evil that occurs in his night will reach him, and no good that occurs in his night will escape him." [In the copy of Isfahan: "in his day."] (Ibid.) And Ibrahim, the Friend of God (peace be upon him), used to say it six times every day and night.

﴿Have they not reflected within themselves? God did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and for a specified term﴾. He means: until a known time, when they reach it and perish, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Indeed, many of the people are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord﴾. ﴿Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them, who were greater than them in strength, and who stirred up the earth﴾, meaning they plowed it, turned it over for cultivation and construction,

﴿and they cultivated it more than these have cultivated it, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they did not believe﴾, so God, Mighty and Majestic, destroyed them.

﴿God would not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾. ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst﴾, meaning the outcome that will distress them, which is the Fire. It was said that al-Su'a is a name for Jahannam, just as al-Husna is a name for Paradise.

﴿That they denied﴾, meaning "because they denied." It was also said that the explanation of al-Su'a is what follows it, namely His saying ﴿that they denied﴾, meaning: then the end of the evildoers was denial, as those evil deeds led them to deny ﴿the signs of God and to mock them﴾, that is, they mocked them.

﴿God originates creation, then repeats it, then to Him you will be returned﴾. ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will be dismayed﴾.

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid, who said: "yublisu" means "they will be grieved." Abu Yahya narrated from him: "they will be disgraced." Qatadah, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it is with two yas. Ibn Zayd said: the mublis is one upon whom calamity and evil have descended. Al-Farra' said: their speech and arguments will be cut off. Abu 'Ubaydah said: they will regret, and he recited:

"O friend, do you recognize a worn-out traced ruin?
He said: Yes, I recognize it, and it has become dismayed."

(Al-Sihah of al-Jawhari: 3/909.)

Al-Sulami read yubalasu with a fatha on the lam, but the first reading is better. ﴿And they will have no intercessors from their partners﴾, meaning their idols that they worshipped besides God, to intercede for them, ﴿and they will be disbelievers in their partners﴾, denying them and disowning them.

﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, on that Day they will be separated﴾. ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a meadow, a garden, delighted﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: they will be honored. Mujahid and Qatadah said: they will be given blessings. Abu 'Ubaydah said: they will be made joyful, and from this it is said: every hibrah is followed by an 'ibrah. Al-'Ajjaj said:

"So praise be to God, who gave the hibr
to the allies of truth; indeed the ally is grateful."

That is, joy. Some of them said: the hibrah in the language is every good blessing. Al-tahbir is beautification, and from it the ink is called hibr, because the pages are beautified with it. The scholar is called hibr because he is characterized by good character. The poet said: "the scribe of Himyar beautifies it." It was also said: yuhbarun means they are made to enjoy listening.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, from Hamid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Yunus, from Rawh, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, regarding ﴿in a meadow, they will be delighted﴾, that he said: "Listening (to music) in Paradise."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Abdullah ibn Shanbah, from Umayr ibn Mirdas, from Salamah ibn Shabib, from Abd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I heard al-Awza'i say regarding ﴿in a meadow, they will be delighted﴾: "Listening." And he said: when listening begins, no tree in Paradise remains except that it rustles. And from him, from Salamah ibn Shabib, from Dawud ibn al-Jarrah al-Asqalani, who said: I heard al-Awza'i say: "None of those whom God created has a more beautiful voice than Israfil. When he begins listening, he cuts off the prayers and glorification of the people of the seven heavens."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dinawari informed us, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Majah al-Qazwini, from al-Hasan ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn 'Arad al-Shaybani, who both said: al-Qasim ibn Mutayyab al-'Ijli informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Paradise has one hundred degrees; between each two degrees is what is between the heaven and the earth. Al-Firdaws is the highest of them in elevation and the middle of them in place, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth, and above it the Throne will be placed on the Day of Resurrection." (Musnad Ahmad: 5/321; Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/82.)

A man stood up to him and said: "O Messenger of God, I am a man to whom voice is beloved; is there a beautiful voice in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, by the One in whose hand is my soul. God, glory be to Him, will reveal to a tree in Paradise: 'Make my servants who occupied themselves with my worship and remembrance hear (the sound), away from the strumming of lutes and the flutes.' Then it will raise a voice that the creatures have never heard the like of, of glorifying and sanctifying the Lord."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Harun, from Muhammad ibn Harun al-'Attar, from Hazim ibn Yahya al-Halawani, from al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik, from Masruh al-Harrani, from Sulayman ibn 'Ata', from Salamah ibn Abdullah al-Juhani, from his paternal uncle, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to admonish the people, and he mentioned Paradise and what is in it of spouses and blessings. At the back of the people was a Bedouin, who knelt on his knees and said: "O Messenger of God, is there any listening in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, O Bedouin. In Paradise there is a river whose banks are virgins of every fair-skinned, slender-waisted kind, who sing with voices the creatures have never heard the like of. That is the best bliss of the people of Paradise." (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 14/13.)

He said: I asked Abu al-Darda': "With what will they sing?" He said: "With glorification, God willing." He said: al-Khawsaniyyah is the one whose upper part is slender and whose lower part is full.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadhani, from Ali ibn Sa'id al-'Askari, who said: Abu Badr 'Abbad ibn al-Walid al-Ghubari informed me, from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khurasani, from Abdullah ibn 'Arada al-Shaybani, from al-Qasim ibn Mutayyab, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: "In Paradise there are trees upon which are bells of silver. When the people of Paradise wish to listen, God, Mighty and Majestic, sends a wind from beneath the Throne, which falls upon those trees, and it moves those bells with sounds that, if the people of the earth heard them, would die of delight." (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 14/13.)

Al-Husayn informed me, from Abu Shanbah and Abdullah ibn Yusuf, who both said: Muhammad ibn 'Imran said, from Muhammad ibn Mansur, who said: Yahya ibn Abi al-Hajjaj informed me, from Abdullah ibn Muslim, from a client of the Banu Umayyah called Sulayman, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah being asked: "Is there any listening for the people of Paradise?"

He said: "Yes. There is a tree whose root is of gold, whose branches are of silver, and whose fruit is pearls, chrysolite and rubies. God, glory be to Him and exalted, sends a wind that makes its parts strike one another, and no one has ever heard anything more beautiful than it."

His saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought to punishment﴾. ﴿So exalted is God﴾, pray to God ﴿when you enter the evening﴾, which is the prayer of 'Asr and Maghrib, ﴿and when you enter the morning﴾, which is the prayer of Fajr. ﴿And to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth﴾, ﴿and in the late afternoon﴾, which is the prayer of 'Isha' al-Akhirah, meaning: glorify Him in the late afternoon, ﴿and when you reach noon﴾, which is the prayer of Zuhr.

He said: "Yes: ﴿So exalted is God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ … to His saying: ﴿and when you reach noon﴾."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ibn Shanbah [in another copy: from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Mahan, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi], from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tayalisi [in the copy of Isfahan: al-Tanafisi], from Yahya ibn Adam, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd al-'Ammi, from Muhammad ibn Wasi', from Ka'b, who said: "Whoever says when he enters the morning: 'Glory be to God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning,' up to the end of the verse, no good that occurs in his day will escape him, and no evil that occurs in it will reach him. And whoever says it when he enters the evening, no evil that occurs in his night will reach him, and no good that occurs in his night will escape him." [In the copy of Isfahan: "in his day."] (Ibid.) And Ibrahim, the Friend of God (peace be upon him), used to say it six times every day and night.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 30, verse 19–27:

﴿He brings the living out of the dead, and brings the dead out of the living, and revives the earth after its death. And thus you will be brought forth.﴾ And among His signs is that He created you from dust, meaning Adam (peace be upon him).

﴿Then, behold, you are human beings dispersing﴾, meaning his descendants.

And among His signs is that He created for you, from yourselves, spouses of your own kind, and did not make them of the jinn. It was also said: from Adam's rib. And it was said: from the drops (nutfah) of men.

﴿And He placed between you affection (mawaddah) and mercy (rahmah)﴾, meaning affection and love.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.﴾

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ali, who said: Abu Shu'ayb al-Harrani informed me, from Yahya ibn Abdullah al-Babili, from Safwan ibn Amr, from al-Mashyakha (the elders), that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Prophet of Allah, I have been amazed at a matter, and it is indeed amazing: a man marries a woman without having seen her, and she has not seen him at all, until he consummates the marriage with her, and they accompany one another, and nothing is more beloved to them than each other."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ﴿And He placed between you affection and mercy﴾.

And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your languages, Arab and non-Arab.

﴿And the difference of your colors: white, black and red.﴾ You are all children of one man and one woman.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge.﴾ Hafs reads the lam with a kasra; al-Yaqut reads it with a fatha.

And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.﴾ And among His signs is that He shows you the lightning, as fear and as hope, and sends down water from the sky, by which He revives the earth after its death. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who use reason.﴾ The "that" (an) has been omitted from His words ﴿He shows you﴾ because the context indicates it, like the words of Tarafah:

Surely, O you who rebukes me, to attend the battle... and if I witness the pleasures, will you make me immortal?

He meant: "that I attend." It was also said: it is on the principle of inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), its meaning being: "and He shows you the lightning, as fear and hope, among His signs."

And among His signs is that the heavens and the earth stand by His command. Then, when He calls you with a single call from the earth, that is, from your graves, according to Ibn Abbas, ﴿behold, you come forth﴾ from it. Most scholars hold that the meaning of the verse is: ﴿Then, when He calls you with a single call from the earth, behold, you come forth from the earth.﴾

﴿To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are obedient to Him.﴾ ﴿And it is He who originates creation, then repeats it.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud read: "yubdi" (He brings forth), and its evidence is His words: ﴿Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats﴾ [Surah al-Buruj: 13].

The evidence of the common reading is ﴿As He originated you, you will return﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 29], and ﴿And it is easier for Him﴾ [Surah al-Rum: 27]. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym and al-Hasan said: "And it is easy for Him, and nothing is difficult for Him," and this is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. This is like the words of al-Farazdaq:

Indeed He who raised the sky for us, a house whose pillars are mighty and lofty.

That is, "mighty and lofty."

Another said:

By your life, indeed al-Zibriqan is generous with his kindness in times of hardship, and most excellent.

That is, "most excellent."

Mujahid and Ikrimah said: "Repetition is easier for Him than initiation," that is, more facile. This is the narration of al-Wali from Ibn Abbas. The sense of this interpretation is that this is a parable God struck: He says, "Restoring a thing to creation is easier than originating it, so resurrection should be easier for Him in your estimation than creation." Some people said: ﴿And it is easier for Him﴾ means, for the creatures: a cry is raised among them and they arise, and it is said to them, "Be!" and they are, which is easier for them than being drops, then clots, then lumps, until they become men and women. This is the meaning of the narration of Hassan, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and the choice of Qutrub.

﴿And to Him belongs the highest likeness in the heavens and the earth.﴾ That is, the most exalted attribute. Ibn Abbas said: "There is nothing like unto Him." Qatadah said: "His likeness is that there is no god but Him, and no lord other than Him." ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

ʿIkrimah and Mujahid said: "There is no altering of the creation of Allah among the animals, such as by castration or the like."

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from ʿAbd al-Razzaq, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah; then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to an animal. Do you see any mutilation in it?" [174] [In the source: "tará" (you see).] [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī: 2/104.] He said: Then Abu Hurayrah would say: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿the fitrah of Allah upon which He created mankind﴾," to the end of the verse.

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Muṭayri informed me, from Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muʾaddib, from ʿAbd al-Razzaq. And Abu Saʿid al-Tajir informed us, saying: Abu Hamid al-Sharqi informed me, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Bishr, and al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq said, from Maʿmar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There is no child born except upon this fitrah, then his parents make him a Jew or a Christian, just as you produce an animal. Do you find in it any mutilation, until you yourselves mutilate it?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say of one who dies while young?" He said: "Allah knows best what they would have done." [175] [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī: 7/211.]

Al-Aswad ibn Sariʿ said: "I fought alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) four campaigns, and a people were killing the offspring. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'What is the matter with people who kill the combatants and then target the offspring?'" A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are only the children of polytheists." He (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, the best of you are the children of polytheists. By Him in whose hand is my soul, there is no child born except upon the fitrah, and it remains upon it until his tongue speaks clearly; then his parents make him a Jew or a Christian." [176] [Musnad Aḥmad: 4/24. The latter part of the ḥadīth is in al-Mustadrak of al-Ḥākim: 2/123, and likewise in al-Sunan al-Kubrā: 9/130, with slight variation.]

Qatadah narrated from Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhīr, from ʿIyad ibn Himar al-Mujashiʿi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah [in the source: 'my Lord'] commanded me to teach you what you do not know, of what He taught me on this day, and that He said: 'Indeed every property I have granted to My servants is lawful to them. I created all My servants as ḥunafāʾ (upright in monotheism), but the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, made unlawful for them what I had made lawful, and commanded them to associate with Me what I had not sent down any authority for.'" [177] [Musnad Aḥmad: 4/162.] And he mentioned the ḥadīth.

Abu Bakr al-Warrāq said: ﴿the fitrah of Allah upon which He created mankind﴾ is poverty and neediness. ﴿That is the upright religion,﴾ the straight one, ﴿but most people do not know.﴾

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿turning in repentance to Him﴾ [In the Isfahan copy there is an addition: "returning to Him in repentance, turning to Him in obedience. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) and as a detached epithet (qaṭʿ), meaning: so set your face, you and your community, turning in repentance to Him."] ﴿and fear Him, and establish the prayer, and do not be among the polytheists, of those who divided their religion and became sects﴾, i.e., divisions, like the Jews and the Christians.

Ibn Fanjawayh [in the Isfahan copy: "Akhbaranī Ibn Fanjawayh"] al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Dīnawarī informed me, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn Isḥāq ibn Ḥabīsh al-Kalwadhānī, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Sulaymān ibn al-Ashʿath, from Muḥammad ibn Muṣaffā, from Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd, from Shuʿbah or another, from Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbi, from Shurayḥ, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to ʿĀʾishah: "O ʿĀʾishah, those who divided their religion and became sects (wa-kānū shiyaʿan), they are the people of innovation and misguidance from this community. O ʿĀʾishah, every person with a sin has repentance, except the people of innovation and desires; for them there is no repentance. I am free of them and they are free of me." [178] [al-Durr al-Manthūr: 3/63, at the verse; and Kitāb al-Sunnah of Abu ʿĀṣim: 8, no. 4.]

Qatadah narrated from Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhīr, from ʿIyad ibn Himar al-Mujashiʿi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah [in the source: 'my Lord'] commanded me to teach you what you do not know, of what He taught me on this day, and that He said: 'Indeed every property I have granted to My servants is lawful to them. I created all My servants as ḥunafāʾ (upright in monotheism), but the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, made unlawful for them what I had made lawful, and commanded them to associate with Me what I had not sent down any authority for.'" [177] [Musnad Aḥmad: 4/162.] And he mentioned the ḥadīth.

Abu Bakr al-Warrāq said: ﴿the fitrah of Allah upon which He created mankind﴾ is poverty and neediness. ﴿That is the upright religion,﴾ the straight one, ﴿but most people do not know.﴾

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿turning in repentance to Him﴾ [In the Isfahan copy there is an addition: "returning to Him in repentance, turning to Him in obedience. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) and as a detached epithet (qaṭʿ), meaning: so set your face, you and your community, turning in repentance to Him."] ﴿and fear Him, and establish the prayer, and do not be among the polytheists, of those who divided their religion and became sects﴾, i.e., divisions, like the Jews and the Christians.

Ibn Fanjawayh [in the Isfahan copy: "Akhbaranī Ibn Fanjawayh"] al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Dīnawarī informed me, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn Isḥāq ibn Ḥabīsh al-Kalwadhānī, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Sulaymān ibn al-Ashʿath, from Muḥammad ibn Muṣaffā, from Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd, from Shuʿbah or another, from Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbi, from Shurayḥ, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to ʿĀʾishah: "O ʿĀʾishah, those who divided their religion and became sects (wa-kānū shiyaʿan), they are the people of innovation and misguidance from this community. O ʿĀʾishah, every person with a sin has repentance, except the people of innovation and desires; for them there is no repentance. I am free of them and they are free of me." [178] [al-Durr al-Manthūr: 3/63, at the verse; and Kitāb al-Sunnah of Abu ʿĀṣim: 8, no. 4.]

﴿Every faction, in what they have, rejoicing.﴾ His saying: ﴿And when harm touches people, they call upon their Lord, turning to Him in repentance; then when He lets them taste mercy from Him…﴾ — abundance and blessing — ﴿…behold, a group of them associate others with their Lord,﴾ ﴿so that they may disbelieve in what We have given them. So enjoy yourselves; you will soon know.﴾ In the codex of ʿAbd Allah it is: "wa-liyatamattaʿū" (and let them enjoy). ﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority?﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: a proof and an excuse. Qatadah and al-Rabīʿ said: a book.

﴿So it speaks﴾, i.e., it speaks out, ﴿of what they used to associate with Him.﴾ It excuses them for their polytheism and commands them to it.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 30, verses 36–53:**

﴿And when We let people taste mercy, they rejoice in it. But if an evil befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth, behold, they despair.﴾ ﴿Have they not seen that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ ﴿So give to the relative his right, and to the needy and the traveler. That is better for those who desire the Face of Allah, and it is they who are the successful.﴾

**His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And what you give in usury (riba)﴾.** Ibn Kathir read *ātaytum* (آتيتم) as a short, unlengthened form. [Al-Hasan, ʿIkrimah and the people of Madina read *li-tarbū* (لتربوا) with a dammed *tā'* and a jazmed *wāw*, in the second person, meaning "that you may increase." This is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbas, and it was chosen by Yaʿqub, Ayyub and Abu Hatim.]

The others read *li-yarbuwa* (ليربوا) with an open *yā'* and a fatha on the *wāw*, making the verb refer to *al-riba*. Abu ʿUbayd preferred this reading because of His saying ﴿so it does not increase with Allah﴾, and He did not say "is not increased."

The exegetes differed about the meaning of the verse. Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Tawus, Qatada and al-Dahhak said: it is a man who gives a gift or presents a present so that he may be repaid with more than it. This is lawful usury, in which there is neither reward nor sin. This applies to people in general, but for the Prophet (ﷺ) specifically it was forbidden, because of the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and do not give out of desire for more﴾.

Al-Shaʿbi said: it is a man who attaches himself to another man, serves him and travels with him, and so he gives him a share of his wealth in order to be repaid, and he gave it only to seek his help and did not intend the Face of Allah.

Al-Nakhaʿi said: this is about a man who says to another, "I will certainly enrich you," and so he gives him out of consideration. In the Jahiliyya, a man would give his relatives wealth so that his own wealth would increase. This is also the narration of Abu Husayn [in the Isfahan manuscript: Abu Husn] from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Al-Suddi said: it was revealed concerning Thaqif, who used to give usury.

﴿So it does not increase with Allah﴾: it does not grow, because it was not intended for the Face of Allah. ﴿And what you give in zakat, desiring the Face of Allah — those are the ones who multiply (al-muḍʿifun)﴾. Qatada said: this is what Allah accepts and multiplies for him ﴿tenfold and more﴾.

The meaning of *al-muḍʿifun* (المضعفون) is "those who have multiplication." It is like the Arabs' saying, "You have become fattened (*musammanīn*)" when their camels grew fat, and "thirsty (*muʿaṭṭashīn*)" when they became thirsty. A man is called *muqwin* when his camels are strong, and *muḍʿif* when they are weak. From this comes *al-khabīth al-mukhabbith*, meaning that its owners are corrupt.

﴿Allah is He who created you, then provided for you, then causes you to die, then gives you life. Is there any of your partners who does any of that? Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate.﴾

**His saying: ﴿Corruption has appeared﴾**, meaning: the rain has been withheld, the crops have decreased, and blessing has departed. ﴿On land and sea﴾: one says, "the land has become barren," and "the sea's source has been cut off." ﴿Because of what the hands of people have earned﴾: because of the evil of their sins.

Qatada said: this was before Allah sent His Prophet (peace be upon him). The earth was filled with injustice and error. When Allah the Mighty and Majestic sent Muhammad (ﷺ), some of the people turned back.

"Land" refers to the people of the ʿamud (tent-poles), the deserts and the open plains, and "sea" refers to the people of the settled areas and villages. Mujahid said: "By Allah, it is not your sea that you know, but every town on flowing water is a sea." ʿIkrima said: the Arabs call the cities "seas." ʿAtiyya and others said: "land" is the surface of the earth, including cities and other places, and "sea" is the well-known sea. ʿAtiyya also said: when the rain decreases, the diving (for pearls) decreases.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: when the sky rains, the shells open their mouths in the sea, and whatever falls into them of rainwater becomes pearl. Al-Hasan said: "the sea" means the villages on the seashore.

Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrima and Mujahid said: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land﴾ through the killing of Adam's son of his brother, ﴿and on the sea﴾ through the tyrannical king who used to seize every ship by force. His name was al-Jalanda, a man of the Azd.

**﴿So that He may let them taste﴾** (*li-yudhīqahum*): al-Sulami read it with a *nūn* (لنذيقهم), and this is the choice of Abu Hatim. The rest read it with a *yā'*. ﴿Some of what they did﴾ means: the punishment for some of the sins they committed. ﴿So that they may return﴾ from their disbelief and their corrupt deeds.

﴿Say: Travel through the earth and see what was the end of those before you. Most of them were polytheists.﴾ ﴿So set your face toward the upright religion, before there comes a Day from Allah that cannot be turned back. On that Day they will be separated (yaṣṣaddaʿun)﴾, meaning: they will scatter. ﴿A party in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.﴾ ﴿Whoever disbelieves, his disbelief is upon him, and whoever does righteousness, it is for their own souls that they prepare (yamhadun)﴾, meaning: they spread out and prepare beds in the graves. ﴿So that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds from His bounty﴾, meaning from His reward. ﴿Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers.﴾

**His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bringers of good news﴾**, and ﴿to let you taste His mercy﴾, meaning His blessing of rain, ﴿and that the ships may sail by His command, and that you may seek of His bounty﴾, meaning His provision, ﴿and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾ ﴿And We certainly sent before you messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs. Then We took vengeance on those who committed crimes﴾, meaning those who associated others with Allah. ﴿And it was truly incumbent upon Us to help the believers.﴾

[Meaning: as We gave them victory at the end, so too We will help you and grant you triumph over those who oppose and oppose you.] Al-Hasan said: it means that He saved them with the messengers from the punishment of their peoples.

Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Abu al-ʿAbbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Sarsari said, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Muṭabbaqi, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Sulayman, from ʿAli ibn Maʿbad, from Musa ibn Aʿyan, from Bashir ibn Abi Sulayman, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from Shahr ibn Hawshab [from Umm al-Darda'], from Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No person defends the honour of his brother except that it is a right upon Allah, glorified is He, to ward off from him the Fire of Hell on the Day of Resurrection." [179] [Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 3/418, with slight variation.] Then he recited this verse: ﴿And it was truly incumbent upon Us to help the believers.﴾

﴿Allah is He who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds﴾. Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Mukhallad al-Baqirhi, from al-Hasan ibn ʿAlawiyya, from Isma'il ibn ʿIsa, from Ishaq ibn Bishr, who said: Idris Abu al-Ilyas informed us, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, that the earth complained to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, during the days of the Flood, because Allah sent the water without measure or weight. The water came out in anger for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and it scratched and gouged the earth. The earth said: "O Lord, the water has gouged and scratched me." Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said, as it has reached me, and Allah knows best: "I will make for the water a sieve that will not gouge or scratch you." So He made the cloud the sieve of the rain.

﴿So He spreads it in the sky however He wills﴾: the pronoun returns to the word "cloud," which is why it is mentioned. "Cloud" (*sahāb*) is a collective noun, as one says, "This is good dates (*tamr*)." ﴿And makes it fragments (kisafan)﴾, meaning scattered pieces. ﴿Then you see the rain (al-wadq) coming out from its midst (khilalihi)﴾, meaning from its center. Ibn ʿAbbas read *min khilalihi* (من خلله).

﴿Then when He strikes with it﴾, meaning with the rain, ﴿whom He wills of His servants, behold, they rejoice﴾. ﴿And even though they were, before it was sent down upon them, before it, certainly in despair (mublisin)﴾. It was also said: "and they were not except..." Qatrub said: the purpose of repeating *qabl* (قبل) here is that the first refers to the sending down and the second to the rain. It was also said that it is for emphasis, like the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they did not do — do not think them safe from punishment﴾ [Al ʿImran: 188]. Here *tahsabanna* (تحسبن) is repeated for emphasis.

The poet said:

*"When I did not trust you, and your meeting was not except from behind a barrier of barriers."* [al-Sihah: 6/2523]

In the reading of Ibn Masʿud: *lā taḥsabanna alladhīna yafraḥūna bimā ātaw* ... "do not think" without repetition, and in his reading also: *wa in kānū min qabli an yunazzala ʿalayhim la-mublisīn* without repetition.

**His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So look at the traces (āthār) of Allah's mercy﴾.** Ahl al-Sham and al-Kufa read *āthār* in the plural, with an *alif*. There is a difference of narration on this from Asamm; others read *athar* in the singular. ﴿Meaning the rain.﴾ ﴿How He gives life to the earth after its death. Indeed, that is the One who gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent,﴾ meaning concerning resurrection and other things.

﴿And if We send a wind, cold and harmful, that ruins what the rain has made grow, they see it﴾, meaning the crops and vegetation, which is a reference to what is not mentioned, ﴿yellowed (muṣfarran)﴾, dry after its greenness and freshness, ﴿they would certainly continue to disbelieve after it﴾, even though they have seen these clear signs. Then He gave them an example, and said: ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs in retreat. Nor can you guide the blind away from their error. You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs, and they are submitting.﴾

﴿And when We let people taste mercy, they rejoice in it. Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Tawus, Qatada and al-Dahhak said: it is a man who gives a gift or presents a present so that he may be repaid with more than it. Al-Nakhaʿi said: this is about a man who says to another, "I will certainly enrich you," and so he gives him out of consideration. Al-Suddi said: it was revealed concerning Thaqif, who used to give usury.

Mujahid said: "By Allah, it is not your sea that you know, but every town on flowing water is a sea." ʿIkrima said: the Arabs call the cities "seas." ʿAtiyya and others said: "land" is the surface of the earth, including cities and other places, and "sea" is the well-known sea. ʿAtiyya also said: when the rain decreases, the diving (for pearls) decreases.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 30, verse 54–60:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is Allah who created you in weakness﴾ [a drop of semen], ﴿then made after weakness strength﴾ [youth], ﴿then made after strength weakness and gray hair﴾ [old age]. Yahya, ʿAsim, al-Aʿmash and Hamzah read the ḍād in "ḍaʿf" (weakness) with a fatḥah (ḍaʿf), while others read it with a ḍammah throughout. Abu ʿUbayd chose the ḍammah because it is the dialect (lughah) of the Prophet (ﷺ).

We were informed by ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan, from Hamid ibn Muhammad, from ʿAli ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, who said, Abu Nuʿaym said, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from ʿAtiyyah al-ʿAwfi, who said: I recited to Ibn ʿUmar ﴿It is Allah who created you in weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness﴾, meaning with the ḍammah. Then he said: I recited it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he took it from me as I have taken it from you.

ʿAsim al-Jahdari used to read ﴿Allah who created you in weakness, then made after weakness﴾ with a ḍammah, ﴿strength, then made after strength weakness﴾ with a fatḥah, wishing to combine the two dialects. al-Farra' said: the ḍammah is the dialect of Quraysh, and the fatḥah is the dialect of Tamim.

﴿He creates what He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful﴾.

And His saying: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear that they did not remain [in the world] except an hour﴾ [Yunus 45]. The people belittled the term of the worldly life when they witnessed the Hereafter. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it means they did not remain in their graves except an hour; they belittled it in view of the terror of the Day of Resurrection. A parallel to it is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿As if they had not remained but an hour of a day﴾ [Yunus 45], ﴿thus they were deluded﴾, i.e., they lied in the world.

﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say: "You have indeed remained within the Book of Allah"﴾, i.e., in what Allah had written for you in His foreknowledge. It is also said: in the decree of Allah, as in the poet's saying:

"The loyalty turned with the affliction, so you turned; and that was not what Allah said when He was writing."

i.e., He decrees. Qatadah and Muqatil said: this is one of the inverted (muqaddam wa mu'akhkhar) constructions of speech; its interpretation is: "And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, 'You have indeed remained, in the Book of Allah, until the Day of Resurrection. This is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not know'" in the world that it would occur, and that you would be resurrected and recompensed, "so you used to deny it."

﴿So on that Day, the excuses of those who wronged will not benefit them, nor will they be asked to make amends﴾, i.e., be restored to good favor.

﴿And We have certainly presented to the people in this Qur'an every kind of example. And if you brought them a sign, those who disbelieve would surely say, "You are not but falsifiers"﴾, i.e., you are upon nothing but falsehood. ﴿Thus does Allah seal the hearts of those who do not know.﴾ ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and let them not disquiet you﴾, i.e., let them not make you slip or make light of your opinion regarding your judgment, ﴿those who have no certainty﴾.

The people belittled the term of the worldly life when they witnessed the Hereafter.
